tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...'), focuses on user-facing trigger scenarios (call fails with access/validation/throttling error, model may be end-of-life, KB returns nothing or stale answers, etc.) rather than implementation details, explicitly covers cases where the user doesn't name the domain directly ('even if they do not mention invocation logging, IAM, service control policies...'), and while long, it is a single cohesive paragraph appropriate for the breadth of scenarios covered.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when a Bedrock call fails with an access, validation or throttling error, when nobody can see what the model is doing, when a model may be end-of-life or an inference profile is in question, or when someone asks whether Bedrock is set up correctly; and when a knowledge base returns nothing or stale answers...

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body avoids explaining general concepts (e.g., what IAM or a knowledge base is) and sticks to domain-specific routing, guardrails and severity definitions that an agent would not otherwise know. It is fairly dense but each sentence carries project-specific signal (check-ids, masking rules, read-only constraints).
tests.evidence: Every finding is grounded in a catalog under `references/` with a stable check-id, a severity and an AWS-doc citation.

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: No large reference tables (API docs, error codes, metric thresholds) are embedded in the body; detailed catalogs and procedures are consistently pushed to references/ files, with only short routing tables and severity definitions kept inline.
tests.evidence: `references/model-access-review.md`: the model access and configuration review (router, procedure, checks before presenting, LLM-INV family, wrong answers, error handling, AWS docs).

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Every file in references/ is linked via markdown link syntax in the References section and/or the routing table.
tests.evidence: `references/model-access-review.md`, `references/knowledge-base-review.md`, `references/checks-model-invocation.md`, `references/checks-rag-knowledgebase.md`, `references/diagnosis-playbook.md`, `references/rag-review-playbook.md`, `references/collection-reference.md`, `references/metrics-and-logs.md`, `references/api-quirks.md`, `references/related-skills.md` are all linked with markdown syntax in the References section.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: The references table and surrounding text specify when each file should be read (e.g., based on the question area, or when encountering a specific error type), rather than generic 'see for details' phrasing.
tests.evidence: Name the area, then read its review file **before the first API call**... | `references/model-access-review.md` | ... AccessDeniedException or a validation error on InvokeModel/Converse...

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference paths use relative 'references/filename.md' format with no absolute paths or traversals.
tests.evidence: `references/model-access-review.md`: the model access and configuration review...

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile, risk-laden operations (account ID masking, read-only guardrails, chunk content suppression) are stated as strict non-negotiable rules, while flexible areas (how to run the review, related skills handling) allow agent judgment with explained rationale.
tests.evidence: **Read-only.** Never call a mutating API. Recommend the fix, state the exact CLI or IaC change and let the user run it.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The routing table gives a clear default path per question type rather than listing many equal options; no competing tool menus are presented without a default.
tests.evidence: | The question is about | Area | Read first | Report template |

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable approach (pick area, read file, run checks, apply guardrails, render report) applicable to any Bedrock review request, not a one-off instance.
tests.evidence: Name the area, then read its review file **before the first API call**. Each file holds the router, the step-by-step procedure, the pre-presentation checks...

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill includes concrete gotcha-like guidance embedded throughout (e.g., distinguishing access-denied cases, throttling cases, misleading API behaviors referenced in api-quirks.md), satisfying the intent even without a dedicated 'Gotchas' heading.
tests.evidence: Two cases that look alike belong to different areas: **Access denied.** On `InvokeModel`/`Converse` it is model access (LLM-INV-013/014/015). On an ingestion job or `Retrieve` it is the knowledge base area (LLM-KB-011).

tests.evidence: `assets/bedrock-configuration-report-template.md` and `assets/rag-health-report-template.md`: report formats for each area.

tests.name: Step-by-step guidance
tests.reasoning: The body does not present an ordered, dependent step-by-step procedure itself; it delegates the actual step-by-step procedures to references/ files (diagnosis-playbook.md, rag-review-playbook.md), so no checklist format is required in SKILL.md body.
tests.evidence: Each file holds the router, the step-by-step procedure, the pre-presentation checks, the check family, common wrong answers and error handling for that area.

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: The skill explicitly instructs pre-presentation validation checks (delegated to reference files) and embeds self-check guardrails like evidence requirements and distinguishing measured-zero vs no-data before finalizing output.
tests.evidence: **Evidence or silence.** Every finding cites the concrete value that triggered it. Distinguish "measured zero" from "no data reported" or "no job to read" (`references/api-quirks.md` §10).
